findings.title: Regression-safety story AC is contradicted
findings.problem: Story AC 'existing CodeMie CLI and Claude Code analytics remain unaffected' fails. countTurns now leaves out interrupt, command-output and automatic-prompt lines, so agent.session.summary.turns drops for ordinary Claude Code sessions. Also, while Desktop is connected, withDesktopIdentity (connect-orchestrator.ts) switches proxy start, proxy restart and hook cold starts to the claude-desktop identity, which changes X-CodeMie-Client on non-Desktop traffic and drops the Codex reasoning sanitizer for an oh-my-pi daemon. Both changes match spec items, so the spec and the story AC disagree.
findings.impact: Turn counts for existing Claude Code sessions shift on the analytics dashboards, and other CLI clients sharing the daemon are attributed to claude-desktop. This breaks the regression guarantee the story requires.
findings.recommendation: Get a product decision: either keep countTurns and the Claude Code session turns as they were (move the new exclusion rule to Cowork only) and stop forcing the claude-desktop identity on non-Desktop daemons, or amend the story AC to accept both changes on purpose.
findings.check_notes: Mapped decision present: story owner accepted both changes (turn count fix, Desktop identity) with a non-empty rationale.

findings.title: Desktop gateway check rejects custom key offline
findings.problem: readDesktopGateway accepts the Desktop config's inferenceGatewayApiKey only when it equals the daemon state file's gatewayKey, or DEFAULT_GATEWAY_KEY when there is no state file. clearState (daemon-manager.ts) deletes the state file on every stop. So with the daemon stopped and Desktop connected using a non-default gateway key, the gateway reads as not connected.
findings.impact: proxy start, proxy restart from stopped, and hook cold start then spawn outside Desktop mode, and Cowork collection stops. This is the regression the change is meant to prevent. Only the Desktop: status line shows it.
findings.recommendation: When no daemon state file exists, accept any loopback CodeMie gateway config (or compare against the key the next start will use / the key recorded at connect time) so start, restart and hook cold start stay in Desktop mode; add a test for a stopped daemon with a non-default key.
findings.check_notes: desktop.ts not in changed_files; readDesktopGateway unchanged. Recorded as a story-owner closure with no code change; a kind:code finding needs a source fix in changed_files, so re-triage it as a deci

disposition.rationale: The CLI never makes a gateway key other than the default: every spawn uses the default key and no option or environment variable sets another.

findings.title: New exported functions lack JSDoc
findings.problem: code-quality.md requires JSDoc on all public APIs. The new exports formatDaemonConflict (daemon-conflict.ts:3), emptyCoworkCursor and coworkCursorPath (cowork-cursor.ts:23, 27) have none.
findings.impact: The documented documentation standard is not met for new exported functions, and the standards audit marks code-quality as a blocking partial.
findings.recommendation: Add a one-line JSDoc to formatDaemonConflict, emptyCoworkCursor and coworkCursorPath.
findings.check_notes: HEAD has one-line JSDoc on formatDaemonConflict, emptyCoworkCursor and coworkCursorPath.

findings.title: Last-dropped timestamp can crash proxy status
findings.problem: formatDropLines calls new Date(drop.at).toISOString() with no guard. The at value comes through toOffset/parseDiscard (session-status.ts), which accept any finite positive number with no upper bound. A value past the Date range makes toISOString throw a RangeError.
findings.impact: A corrupt or out-of-range status file breaks proxy status and proxy analytics status output, the commands meant to show delivery problems.
findings.recommendation: Guard the conversion: const d = new Date(drop.at); const when = Number.isFinite(d.getTime()) ? d.toISOString() : String(drop.at); or clamp `at` to the valid Date range in toOffset/parseDiscard.
findings.check_notes: formatDropLines now checks Number.isNaN(at.getTime()) and prints String(drop.at); regression test added.

findings.title: Undeclared backfill env option added
findings.problem: The spec says 'no new option and no new consent; sessions older than 7 days never appear'. The change adds the env option CODEMIE_DESKTOP_ANALYTICS_BACKFILL_DAYS (capped by MAX_BACKFILL_DAYS = 14), which can widen the window to 14 days.
findings.impact: This partly meets an approved spec requirement. Users can widen collection to sessions older than 7 days through an option the spec does not declare.
findings.recommendation: Remove CODEMIE_DESKTOP_ANALYTICS_BACKFILL_DAYS and fix the window at 7 days as the spec states, or get the spec amended to declare the option.
findings.check_notes: Code unchanged; spec.md now declares CODEMIE_DESKTOP_ANALYTICS_BACKFILL_DAYS (verified), but the author amended it. Needs spec-owner approval via a decision.

disposition.rationale: The backfill window variable is declared in the PR description and in docs/ARCHITECTURE-PROXY.md and is covered by a test; it adds no command option and no consent.

findings.title: New functions exceed 50-line limit
findings.problem: code-quality.md says functions stay under 50 lines. The new CoworkEventProducer.process (~70 lines), buildCoworkEvents (~71 lines, cowork-events.ts) and toolEvents (~54 lines) are over it.
findings.impact: The documented code-structure standard is not met for new code. The standards audit treats it as blocking.
findings.recommendation: Split CoworkEventProducer.process, buildCoworkEvents and toolEvents into named helpers (per pass / per event type) so each stays under 50 lines.
findings.check_notes: Functions still over 50 lines. Recorded as a story-owner closure with no code change; a kind:code finding needs a source fix in changed_files, so re-triage it as a decision on a new final round or fix

disposition.rationale: Each of the three functions is one sequential pass; the functions beside them in the same runtime are longer. Splitting them adds risk with no change in behaviour.

findings.title: Backfill window skips orchestrator usage passes
findings.problem: On a cursor-less first run, windowStartMs is passed only to buildCoworkEvents. The orchestrator passes (main, subagent, session-end) read the whole transcript and still emit agent.usage.request for lines older than the window. The test 'builds no producer event older than the window' asserts that msg_synthetic_OLD is sent.
findings.impact: Usage older than the 7-day window is sent. When orchestrator state is lost on a long-lived session, usage older than the backend's 14-day dedupe can be re-sent and counted twice, against the no-duplicates AC. Whether that double-count path is reached in practice was not confirmed.
findings.recommendation: Apply the same windowStartMs to the orchestrator passes (openMainTranscriptPass / openSubagentPass / openSessionEndPass) on a cursor-less first run, so no usage line older than the window is emitted; update the 'builds no producer event older than the window' test so it checks orchestrator events too.
findings.check_notes: CoworkEventProducer.ts unchanged; orchestrator passes still ignore windowStartMs. Recorded as a story-owner closure with no code change; a kind:code finding needs a source fix in changed_files, so re-

disposition.rationale: The window bounds the producer's own events; a session's usage is sent whole so its tokens and cost are complete, and a lost producer cursor alone re-sends none of it.

findings.title: New files break kebab-case naming
findings.problem: code-quality.md Naming Conventions require kebab-case.ts file names. The new files CoworkEventProducer.ts and CoworkRunner.ts use PascalCase. The repo does already have PascalCase files such as DesktopTelemetryRuntime.ts.
findings.impact: The documented naming standard is not met by newly added files. The standards audit treats it as blocking.
findings.recommendation: Rename to cowork-event-producer.ts and cowork-runner.ts and update imports, or record the PascalCase class-file exception in code-quality.md.
findings.check_notes: PascalCase file names kept; code-quality.md not amended. Recorded as a story-owner closure with no code change; a kind:code finding needs a source fix in changed_files, so re-triage it as a decision o

disposition.rationale: The class files of this directory are named after their class, as DesktopTelemetryRuntime.ts and its neighbours are.

findings.title: Cursor seen-uuid set grows without bound
findings.problem: buildCoworkEvents stores every counted line uuid in state.seenUuids = [...seen], and agentResults only grows. Both are kept in the Cowork cursor, which saveCoworkCursor writes out in full on every processing.
findings.impact: For a long-lived Cowork session, the cursor file, the per-run parse and serialize cost, and memory grow without limit on every producer run.
findings.recommendation: Bound the persisted state: keep only uuids at or after the read offsets (or cap at a fixed MAX_SEEN_UUIDS keeping the newest), and prune agentResults entries whose subagent has stopped.
findings.check_notes: cowork-events.ts unchanged; seenUuids still unbounded. Recorded as a story-owner closure with no code change; a kind:code finding needs a source fix in changed_files, so re-triage it as a decision on

disposition.rationale: The transcript orchestrator's own parse state keeps the same uncapped list of seen uuids; the Cowork cursor follows it.
